stem: Which X-ray finding is characteristic of a dislocated hip in a child over 6 months of age?

options.text: A larger ossification center in the affected femoral head
A steeper acetabular roof and lateral displacement of the femoral head

explanation: Dislocated hips often show a more vertical (steeper) cup shape and the femoral head sitting further away from the center of the joint.
rationale: Look for descriptions of the angle of the hip socket and the position of the femur.

optionExplanations.A: A dislocated hip typically presents with a steeper, rather than flattened, acetabular roof.
optionExplanations.B: The ossification center on the dislocated side is usually smaller due to a delay in the ossification process.
optionExplanations.C: Dislocated hips often show a more vertical (steeper) cup shape and the femoral head sitting further away from the center of the joint.
optionExplanations.D: Amniotic fluid is a prenatal factor and cannot be seen or measured on an infant's hip X-ray.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: A steeper acetabular roof and lateral displacement of the femoral head
